## The question

> What does HTTPS actually protect?

**The walkaway:**

> Encryption for the trip and a certificate for the domain: not a promise about the business.

## Script

| # | In | Type | s | Narration | Caption text (board) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 0:00.0 | hook | 4.4 | That little padlock in your browser means something important. | the padlock |
| 2 | 0:04.4 | hook | 3.2 | Just not quite what people think. | not what you think |
| 3 | 0:08.6 | explain | 5.2 | HTTP is the set of rules a browser and a website use to exchange information. | the rules of the trip |
| 4 | 0:13.8 | explain | 5.0 | HTTPS is the same rules over an encrypted connection, usually TLS. | same rules, sealed |
| 5 | 0:18.8 | explain | 5.6 | That stops someone on the network reading or changing what moves between you and the site. | unreadable in the middle |
| 6 | 0:23.4 | explain | 4.8 | The site also presents a certificate, so your browser can check it's the right domain. | a certificate for the domain |
| 7 | 0:28.2 | explain | 4.0 | On a properly configured HTTPS site, your connection has real protection. | the trip is protected |
| 8 | 0:32.2 | myth-check | 4.6 | But here's the catch: a scam website can use HTTPS too. | anyone can have it |
| 9 | 0:37.8 | myth-check | 5.4 | The padlock doesn't promise the business is honest, or the offer is real. | not an honesty badge |
| 10 | 0:42.2 | compare | 4.6 | Think of it as a protected connection, not a trust badge. | connection, not badge |
| 11 | 0:47.8 | recap | 4.8 | An encrypted connection is not an honest website. | ENCRYPTED NOT HONEST |
| 12 | 0:52.6 | outro | 3.4 | HTTPS protects the connection. Check the site too. | THE PADLOCK MYTH |
